# 34_run_pii_checker.sh - Check data files for PII with a local LLM

<!-- BEGIN pipeline-callers: generated by tools/automation_doc_links.py, do not edit by hand -->
:::{attention} Usually run by a Bitbucket pipeline
`34_run_pii_checker.sh` is normally not run on its own. The Bitbucket pipelines listed below call it as one step of a longer job, after earlier steps have prepared its inputs and environment. Run it by hand mainly for debugging or local testing.

## Description

Checks the tabular data files of the deposit for personally identifiable information (PII) with [pii-checker](https://github.com/AEADataEditor/pii-checker), which asks an LLM about every column that might hold PII. The LLM runs in Ollama on the machine that hosts the self-hosted Bitbucket runner, so the data never go to an outside service. The [`p-pii-checker`](#pipeline-p-pii-checker) pipeline runs it on that runner; [Self-hosted runner for the PII check](#self-hosted-runner) explains how to set one up.

The script:

1. Downloads the deposit if its directory is not there, with the downloader for the repository named in `config.yml` (openICPSR, World Bank, Dataverse or Zenodo).
2. Clones pii-checker (branch or tag `PiiCheckerRef`) into a scratch directory and installs its requirements into a virtual environment of its own.
3. Runs `tools/run_pii_checker.py`. It loads the model in Ollama, runs pii-checker with `--strip-details`, and sorts the results.

| File | Contents | Where it goes |
|---|---|---|
| `pii-checker-full/pii_checker_results.xlsx` | All results, including the values from the data that were shown to the model | Build artifact, downloadable from the build's Artifacts tab for 14 days. Never committed (`.gitignore` excludes `pii-checker-full/`) |
| `generated/pii_checker_results-nodetails.xlsx` | The same without the observed values | Committed |
| `generated/pii_checker_summary.txt` | Counts of checked and flagged columns | Committed, and posted to the Jira ticket |

The `reasoning` column, which holds the model's one-sentence explanation, stays in the committed workbook. It normally describes a column in general terms ("contains full names"), but review flagged columns before sharing the workbook further.

Ollama is reached at `OLLAMA_ENDPOINTS` if that is set. Otherwise the script uses port 11434 of the step container's default gateway, which is the runner's host. Ollama on the host must therefore listen on more than `127.0.0.1`. The script loads the model before pii-checker starts: pii-checker's own test call gives up after 30 seconds, and a large model can take longer to load from disk. When pii-checker finishes, it unloads the model.

## Usage

```bash
. ./tools/resolve_project_id.sh
./automations/34_run_pii_checker.sh $projectID
```

### Environment Variables

- `PiiModel` - Ollama model (default: `gemma4:26b`). It must already be pulled on the host.
- `PiiCheckerRef` - Branch or tag of pii-checker (default: `main`).
- `OLLAMA_ENDPOINTS` - Ollama URL, for example `http://192.168.1.4:11434` (default: the default gateway, port 11434).
- `openICPSRID`, `WorldBankID`, `DataverseID`, `ZenodoID` - Set by `tools/resolve_project_id.sh`; used to download the deposit.
- `ICPSR_EMAIL`, `ICPSR_PASS` - For a private openICPSR deposit.

### `tools/run_pii_checker.py`

Can also be run on its own against a pii-checker checkout, with a Python that has pii-checker's requirements:

```bash
python3 tools/run_pii_checker.py 123456 --checker-dir ../pii-checker --model gemma4:26b \
    --endpoint http://localhost:11434 --summary-file generated/pii_checker_summary.txt
```

Options: `--full-dir` (default `pii-checker-full`) and `--output-dir` (default `generated`) set where the two workbooks go.
